subject: External pentest: clarify which hosting variants are in-scope (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Alex Holt <alex.holt@acme-analytics.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@cypherprobe.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: scope confirmation for external penetration test

Hi Sofia,

We're lining up the external penetration test vendor and need to confirm exactly which of Redwood's hosting models are considered in-scope for the standard vendor external test. Specifically:

- Hosted (Redwood multi-tenant hosted API)
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools for customer)
- Private / VPC (customer-deployed or Redwood Private installation inside customer VPC)
- On-prem (customer-managed, air-gapped deployments)

Our vendor (cc'd) is asking whether they should expect to test the shared-hosted endpoints, the dedicated instances, and whether there are restrictions when testing Private/VPC or on-premise deployments. Also attached is our standard vendor request form — please confirm any additional access requirements or redlines.

Goal: define a single scope statement so we can finalize the statement of work and schedule.

Thanks,
Alex Holt
Head of Security
Acme Analytics

Attachments: Acme_Pentest_Request_Form.pdf
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Holt <alex.holt@acme-analytics.com>, security@cypherprobe.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scope confirmation for external penetration test

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and for sharing the form. Quick summary up front: Hosted (our public multi-tenant API) and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools are within the scope of Redwood's external assessment; Private/VPC and fully on-prem installs are handled case-by-case and typically require coordination with the customer.

Details:
- Hosted (public API): Redwood will provide a scope statement for the tenant-facing endpoints. External blackbox testing against production endpoints is common; we can provide test accounts and rate-limited traffic windows.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): These are single-tenant resources but still operated by Redwood. We can permit external vendor testing against customer-dedicated endpoints with constraints — we do not provide host-level root access to the physical or cloud host. Agent-based or container-level tests and authenticated API tests are supported after a brief onboarding.
- Private / VPC: If Redwood is running the control plane but the compute is customer-managed (VPC or on-prem), Redwood cannot directly execute network-level tests inside customer networks. We can provide control-plane logs, API endpoints we manage, and test guidance; the customer must authorize network-level tests and/or provide a staging environment reachable from the vendor.
- On-prem (air-gapped): These are out of scope for Redwood to test directly. Customer must provide evidence/artifacts (audit logs, scan results) or arrange a local vendor engagement.

Requested from you and the vendor:
1) Confirm if you want external blackbox tests against the public Hosted API and which endpoints (ingest vs admin).
2) Confirm if the Dedicated pools you purchased should be treated as in-scope and whether we should open a temporary testing window.
3) If Private/VPC is in-scope, identify the networking approach (peered test VPC or customer-provided bastion) so we can coordinate.

I'll loop in Marcus (infra) and Naomi (security) to confirm what access we can and cannot provide and to prepare the evidence checklist.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: CypherProbe Ops <security@cypherprobe.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Holt <alex.holt@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scope confirmation for external penetration test

Thanks Sofia — that's helpful. A couple of clarifying points from the vendor side:

- For Hosted public endpoints we plan an external blackbox test focused on auth flows, rate-limiting, and common API injection vectors; we typically use non-destructive tests but need a low-traffic window and a test account.
- For Dedicated pools, we expect to be able to validate isolation controls (network ACLs, VPC flow logs, container boundary checks). We do not need host root access for our test plan but will request read-only access to service logs and the ability to run authenticated API tests.
- For Private/VPC, we can work over a peered test VPC or via a customer-provided bastion/jump host; we will provide an IP allowlist and a short checklist for the customer to run pre-test validations.

Proposed schedule: test kickoff week of 2027-06-27 with a 2-week window. We'll share a detailed test plan and an equipment list.

Please tell us what artifacts we can expect from Redwood for Dedicated and Hosted (e.g., routing/network ranges, service account for auth tests, log retention pointers).

Thanks,
CypherProbe Ops
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, security@cypherprobe.com, Alex Holt <alex.holt@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scope confirmation for external penetration test

Looping in infra details. Short answers: what we can provide and what we cannot.

Provided for Dedicated (Redwood-managed):
- VPC/subnet ranges for the customer's dedicated cluster (we will provide IP ranges and ACLs).
- Read-only aggregated service logs (auth events, ingress/egress) for the test window.
- A scoped service account with limited privileges for authenticated API testing.
- A temporary security group rule to allow the vendor IPs during the test window.

Not provided for Dedicated:
- Root/host-level access to the underlying EC2/GCE instance or hypervisor.
- Any tampering with Redwood host security agents or kernel modules.

Private / VPC installs (customer-managed compute):
- We can provide API-level endpoints and control-plane logs (where Redwood operates the control plane).
- For network-level tests inside the customer's VPC, the customer must either: provide a peered staging VPC reachable by the vendor, provide a bastion host with vendor SSH keys, or run the vendor's validated test runner locally and share results.

On-prem / air-gapped:
- We cannot run tests. We'll accept customer-run test reports or coordinate a local vendor engagement.

I'll attach a short access guide for Dedicated that lists the typical artifacts and the process to request temporary allowlist rules.

Attachments: dedicated-access-guide.txt

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Holt <alex.holt@acme-analytics.com>, security@cypherprobe.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scope confirmation for external penetration test

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below.

Summary:
- Hosted: in-scope for external blackbox tests against tenant-facing API endpoints. We'll provide test accounts and a low-traffic window.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): in-scope with restrictions (no host/root access). We'll provide IP ranges, read-only logs, a scoped service account, and a temporary allowlist during the test window.
- Private/VPC: in-scope only if Acme provides a peered staging VPC or bastion; otherwise, customer-run tests or evidence are acceptable.
- On-prem: out of scope for Redwood to execute; customer must coordinate locally.

Next steps (action items):
1) Acme: sign and return the vendor request form (you already attached it) with the boxes checked for Hosted and/or Dedicated.
2) CypherProbe: share the detailed test plan and the vendor IP allowlist by 2027-06-10.
3) Marcus/Infra: once we have the IPs, please prepare the temporary allowlist and the scoped service account; Marcus to confirm readiness by 2027-06-20.
4) Naomi/Security: I'll work with you to assemble the evidence checklist (logs, retention, config snapshots) and share the CSV.

Attaching the initial evidence checklist we'll populate for Acme (redwood-pt-evidence-checklist.csv). If that looks good, I'll convert it into a minimal deliverable pack for the vendor.

Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
